published.note: Published 2026-11-27 from the run's own files. Local paths are anonymised as <evidence>; prices, costs, absolute latencies and host identities are removed (see 'removed'). The harness that ran it (tools/poc-modal at e55df535) and the control plane image (built from 43dbdbf5) are not commits on main, so this records what ran, not a reproduction script in this release.

original_files.role: the harness's run log (traffic shape line)

removed: every price and cost: the rate, budgets and caps, estimated and billed spend, cost per million output tokens, the report's cost metric and monthly section, the campaign's approved spend

absolute latency, time to first token and time per output token in milliseconds (turns, setups, the judge's means, the report, the planner's input signals): the rules publish no absolute latency from these campaigns because it was measured from a laptop through a tunnel; changes, noise floors and the judge's decisions are kept
Modal function-call ids, lease ids, pod names, server URLs and hostnames: replaced by server labels S0 to S5
the cluster's proxy image reference (a local registry hostname) and the local control plane's deployment and revision identifiers

decision: propose Speculative decoding with the model's own prediction head
gpu: 1 x NVIDIA H100 SXM5 80GB on Modal (gpu="H100!")
measured_from: a local Kubernetes (kind) cluster on a laptop running the InferCrane control plane; every request crossed the internet to the GPU servers through a tunnel

current_setup.added_because: vLLM 0.34.0 does not start the publisher's command on one H100: max_num_seqs 1024 exceeds the 904 recurrent-state (Mamba) cache blocks, and vLLM asks for at most 904. A campaign holds at most 32 requests at once, so 512 changes nothing it measures.

replay.trace: Mooncake FAST'25 arxiv trace, first rows, lengths scaled to the run's shape and capped
replay.reasoning: Requests do not switch the model's reasoning off, so it reasons before it answers, as a request without that switch does in production. Output tokens per second count every generated token, reasoning included. The built-in answer check does switch reasoning off for its 24 short prompts and scores word overlap with the current setup's answers (token F1, at most 64 tokens each), not exact text.
